chunks.text:
Hi Maks,
We said enough during your visit. The long walk, the conversation that kept going, the way you laid out where you’re headed and what you’re building. I don’t need to repeat it here.
The visit felt like a compression algorithm: months of scattered signals collapsing into a few hours of clarity. A lot of “I already sensed this” turning into “now I can say it out loud.” You didn’t need convincing.
And the simplest true thing is still the same: you’re capable. The uncertainty you feel sometimes is about whether you’ll let yourself do the thing without getting in your own way.

I’ve watched the growth close up this year. More direct. Less self-interruption. More willingness to ship before you feel ready. That last one is the hardest. You’ve started shipping anyway. I can see it in the way you talk about your work now, the way you’ve stopped hedging.
First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.Epictetus, Discourses III.23

When I say “just do things,” I’m not trying to give you advice. I hate advices, in general. I’m naming what I see you doing when you’re at your best. You pick a direction. You take the next concrete step. You let reality teach you faster than rumination ever will.
I have 100% belief in you. Not 80%, not “probably,” not “if things go well.” One hundred percent. I’ve watched you long enough to know what you’re made of.
I’m proud of you. See you on the other side of whatever you’re building next.
